coursesExamined.name: Econometrics
coursesExamined.evidenceRead: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

relevantTermHits.name: International Macroeconomics
relevantTermHits.content: International Macroeconomics Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment. Understand how governments and central banks use fiscal and monetary policies to influence economic performance over time. The course also explores business cycles, international trade, and economic crises, preparing students to evaluate policy debates and global economic trends. Examines short-, medium- and long-run macroeconomic dynamics and policy, including international dimensions. Students study goods, financial and labour markets, inflation and unemployment, economic growth, expectations and the open economy. IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models connect markets and policy effects. Algebraic and graphical analysis and interpretation of macroeconomic indicators support the evaluation of economic developments and fiscal and monetary policy. Goods and financial markets; Labour markets; Phillips curve; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC models; Economic growth; Saving and capital accumulation; Technological progress; Expectations; Open-economy macroeconomics; Fiscal and monetary policy; Business cycles and economic crises Algebraic and graphical macroeconomic analysis; IS-LM and IS-LM-PC modelling; Macroeconomic data and indicator analysis

relevantTermHits.name: Public Economics
relevantTermHits.content: Public Economics Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity. The course covers taxation, public goods, externalities, and government spending. Combining theoretical models with empirical evidence, it evaluates how different policies affect societal welfare. Examines government intervention through the efficiency and equity effects of public policy. Market failure, public goods and externalities provide foundations for studying public production, collective choice, spending and taxation. Health, education, welfare and social insurance illustrate expenditure and redistribution questions. Students apply economic models, interpret data and graphs, evaluate research and develop a research proposal and paper. Role and size of government; Market efficiency and failure; Public goods; Externalities; Efficiency and equity; Public production; Public choice; Public expenditure; Health and education policy; Welfare programs; Social insurance; Taxation and redistribution Economic model-based policy analysis; Efficiency and equity assessment; Interpretation of economic data and graphs; Critical evaluation of public-economics research

academicJudgment.positiveArgument: The tested 24-course composition contains real public/private/international/EU/criminal/constitutional/business law, economic public-policy analysis and taxation, accounting, macro/microeconomics, empirical research and advocacy. academicJudgment.academicFinding: Fresh evidence does not connect its recurring legal reasoning to taxation as a legal institution: taxable income/profits, VAT, administrative tax assessment/collection, tax remedies or allocation of taxing rights. Public Economics studies incidence/efficiency/equity, not tax-law interpretation. Accounting and finance study statements, appraisal and financial institutions; comparative private/EU/business law does not supply tax doctrine. This missing organising link persists across a full programme, rather than merely one missing specialist course. No law-degree title, Dutch system, credential, exact-equivalence or matching-course quota is required. Do not invent a fiscal research assignment or use optional research to establish core formation.
